invariant: A multi-threaded CFA is a tuple (V, P): V global variables, each process p=(L, l0, A, E) with transitions E ⊆ L×A×L (edge = source loc, target loc, one statement).
reference: Telbisz et al., On-the-fly Cone-of-Influence Reduction for Model Checking Concurrent Software, SPIN'25 (Def. 1)

invariant: A program state stores the CFA locations of all processes plus the values of all variables; a state is an error state iff any process is in an error location.
written(α) holds a single item for an assignment and is empty for a guard condition; conditionals/guards are never simplified (the transitive-observation relation is reflexive).
Action β observes α under precision Π iff written(α) ∩ read(β) ∩ vars(Π) ≠ ∅. Transitive observation over-approximates real data flow (a variable may be rewritten before it is observed).

The abstract data-flow graph G=(A,D,I,Π): D = direct (in-process) observation edges, I = indirect (inter-process) observation edges. Buildable in polynomial (quadratic) time in the number of CFA edges.
reachable(s,p) — the actions process p could execute after state s — is over-approximated by reachability in the CFA of the program.
A direct edge (α1,α2)∈D is enabled in s iff both endpoints are reachable by the same process; an indirect edge (α1,α2)∈I is enabled iff its endpoints are reachable by two different processes.
An action α may be skipped iff there is no trace from the current state in which a 'real observer' (a guard/conditional) transitively observes α.

Soundness: statement simplification via the data-flow slice preserves reachability — the algorithm returns 'unsafe' whenever an error state is reachable in the concrete state space. An over-approximate slice never hides a reachable fault.
A transition system is (S,T), T ⊆ S×S; it is non-terminating (deadlock-free) iff T is total ({s' | (s,s')∈T} ≠ ∅ for every s).
reference: Watanabe et al., A Coalgebraic Representation of Reduction by Cone of Influence, ENTCS 164 (2006) (Def. 2.1)

invariant: R ⊆ S1×S2 is a simulation if every step of M1 is matched by a step of M2 within R; a bisimulation if both R and R⁻¹ are simulations.
A P-coalgebra (S, α:S→PS) is equivalent to a transition system via (s,s')∈T ⇔ s'∈α(s); a coalgebra morphism corresponds to a bisimulation and a lax morphism to a simulation.

COI reduction eliminates variables not related to the verified property by analysing the dependency graph of state variables; the reduced model (bi)simulates the original and so preserves the relevant temporal properties (CTL*/ACTL*).

Static linters are fundamentally rooted in static analysis; their effectiveness is inherently limited by Python's dynamic type system and dynamic features (metaclasses, decorators, dynamic attribute assignment), so they can only approximate behavior.
reference: Eghbali, Burk & Pradel, DyLin: A Dynamic Linter for Python, Proc. ACM Softw. Eng. 2 (FSE'25), Art. FSE125 (§1)

invariant: Static and dynamic analysis are complementary: dynamic linting operates on actual executions, avoiding the approximations Python's dynamism imposes on static tools, and detects problems missed statically.
Runtime verification monitors program executions against formal specifications (FSM/LTL/ERE), complementing testing by catching violations that assertions do not encode.
reference: Shen et al., PyMOP: A Runtime Verification Tool for Python, FSE Companion '26 (Abstract, §1)

invariant: TOCTOU (Time-Of-Check-To-Time-Of-Use) spans a check (e.g. os.access(f)) and a use (open(f)) across calls; verifying such behavioral properties statically needs inter-procedural analysis and is hard — a motivating case for runtime/heuristic checks over static proof.
An enabled step Y transforms M1 into M2 where, for every place p, M2(p) = (M1(p) − Σ_{(t,b)∈Y} E(p,t)<b>) + Σ_{(t,b)∈Y} E(t,p)<b>.
reference: Jensen, An Introduction to the Theoretical Aspects of Coloured Petri Nets, DAIMI PB-476, 1994 (Definition 3.6)

invariant: The occurrence of a step is indivisible: there is no intermediate marking with inputs removed but outputs not yet added.
An occurring transition changes only the markings of places connected to it by an arc.
reference: Jensen, Kristensen & Wells, Coloured Petri Nets and CPN Tools for Modelling and Validation of Concurrent Systems, STTT 2007 (author manuscript, Sect. 2.2)

invariant: The marking reached by a step of concurrently enabled binding elements equals the marking reached by letting them occur sequentially in any order.
reference: Jensen, Kristensen & Wells, STTT 2007 (author manuscript, Sect. 2.3)

invariant: A port place and the socket place it is assigned to are views of one compound place and always share the same marking.
reference: Jensen, Kristensen & Wells, STTT 2007 (author manuscript, Sect. 2.4)

invariant: Related port and socket places must have identical colour sets and identical initial markings.
reference: Jensen, Kristensen & Wells, STTT 2007 (author manuscript, Sect. 2.4)

invariant: A substitution transition is never itself enabled and never occurs; it represents the compound behaviour of its submodule.
reference: Jensen, Kristensen & Wells, STTT 2007 (author manuscript, Sect. 2.4)

invariant: In timed CPN a binding element can occur only when every token it consumes has a time stamp ≤ the current global clock.
reference: Jensen, Kristensen & Wells, STTT 2007 (author manuscript, Sect. 2.5)

invariant: The global clock advances only when no binding element is both colour-enabled and ready, and then to the earliest model time at which one can occur.
reference: Jensen, Kristensen & Wells, STTT 2007 (author manuscript, Sect. 2.5)

invariant: Weights W determine a place invariant iff Σ_p W_p(M(p)) = Σ_p W_p(M0(p)) for every reachable M; a place flow always determines one, and the converse holds when there are no dead binding elements.
Zero places hold no tokens in any stable marking.
reference: Bruni & Montanari, Zero-Safe Nets, or Transition Synchronization Made Simple, ENTCS 7, 1997 (Abstract)

invariant: A stable marking is a multiset over the stable (non-zero) places only.
A stable transaction evolves between two stable markings with no stable intermediate marking and consumes all stable tokens available at its start, so it is atomic as seen from stable places.
A transaction must not consume a stable token produced within the same transaction.
The abstract P/T net of a zero-safe net has the stable places as places and one transition per abstract stable transaction.
Commit and abort take place at the parent, and only a top-level transaction's commit or abort is irreversible, so a subtransaction's commit is relative to its parent.
reference: Lynch & Merritt, Introduction to the Theory of Nested Transactions, MIT/LCS/TR-367, 1986 (Sect. 3)

invariant: T' is visible to T only if every ancestor of T' below lca(T,T') has committed, so a committed child of an aborted parent is invisible outside that parent.
